literal: Always abandoning is necessary, with fame good not-yielding action.
translation: One must always abandon actions that do not yield goodness and fame.
modern: புகழையும் நன்மையையும் தராத செயல்களை ஒருவன் எப்போதும் தவிர்த்தல் வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet sets a clear standard for choosing one's actions. It states that any deed failing to produce both moral goodness and a good reputation must be strictly avoided. The word 'என்றும்' (always) emphasizes that there are no exceptions to this rule, regardless of the situation or potential short-term gains. By commanding 'ஒருவுதல் வேண்டும்' (must be abandoned), the text insists that pure conduct requires rejecting anything that compromises one's honor or virtue.
